findings.title: Spawned workers fail the Process type check and are never killed
findings.body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances. SpawnProcess is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check is false for production workers. When a worker is declared hung, it is therefore left running while a replacement is started and its reference is overwritten. The old worker can resume flushing the same shards concurrently with its replacement, and repeated hangs leak workers. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or distinguish processes from threads another way before killing them.

findings.title: Do not skip cleanup of remaining workers when the join deadline expires
findings.body: When the shared join deadline expires, this break exits the worker loop without terminating any remaining workers. For example, if the first worker consumes the timeout waiting on Kafka, all subsequent workers are abandoned even if they are also blocked. Setting stopped only takes effect when a worker returns to its main loop, so it does not stop workers stuck in Redis or future.result(). During rebalancing these workers can remain alive after replacement flushers start. Apply the deadline only to waiting, and perform termination cleanup for every worker regardless of whether time remains.
